subject: history_social
passage: The Latin word vomitorium is often explained, in jokes and even in some older reference books, as the name of a room where wealthy Romans emptied their stomachs between courses so that they could go on feasting. No such rooms existed, and no Roman writer describes one. ______ a vomitorium was a passageway in a theater or amphitheater through which crowds poured out at the end of a performance; the word comes from the same root as "vomit" only because the building seemed to spew its audience into the street.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The second sentence rejects the popular explanation of the word. The third sentence gives the correct meaning in its place. A transition that replaces a rejected idea with the right one is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The passageway is not an example of a room that never existed; it is the correct meaning that replaces that idea.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "In other words" is tempting because the sentence explains the word, but it does not restate the previous sentence; it gives a different meaning after the previous one was rejected.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Consequently" would mean the real meaning follows from the fact that no such rooms existed, but the real meaning is a separate fact, not a result.
explanation.D: Correct. "Rather" introduces the true meaning of vomitorium in place of the false one the author has just rejected.
